sources.name: Recharged — Tesla Model Y Real-World Highway Range Explained (2025)
Car and Driver — older Long Range AWD steady 75 mph test ~220 mi

narrative_one_liner: Tesla advertises 311 mi (EPA combined); independent tests show 225–255 mi at steady 70 mph (≈22% gap).
narrative: Tesla advertises 311 mi EPA combined for the Model Y Long Range AWD. Independent 70-mph highway tests put real-world range at roughly 225–255 mi — a 20–25% gap. EPA combined averages city + highway driving with weighting that favors lower speeds where EVs are most efficient.
methodology_notes: Recharged synthesizes multiple owner reports and published independent tests at constant highway speeds. Car and Driver reports a single instrumented test at steady 75 mph. Both methodologies represent constant-speed steady-state, distinct from EPA's mixed-cycle.
caveats: EPA combined number varies by wheel size; we use 311 mi (20in) as the most-purchased configuration. With 19in wheels, EPA rises to ~327 mi.
Recharged is a lower-profile publication; its synthesis methodology is documented but not as authoritative as CR.
Car and Driver tested at 75 mph (not 70), making direct comparison to a 70 mph EPA target imperfect.
alternative_explanations: Battery degradation could account for some gap on older units; tests cited use new units, so this is unlikely the primary driver.
Cold weather alone can produce a 20%+ gap; Recharged data is mild-weather, ruling this out.
Tire choice (e.g., All Season vs. Performance) shifts efficiency by 5–10%.
